$comment: Every environment variable a Semiont service written in Rust reads, beside its configuration document (GatewayConfig, DispatcherConfig, ArchivistConfig) and the broker variables that document names (the gateway's signal.userEnv and signal.passwordEnv, the dispatcher's queue.userEnv and queue.passwordEnv). A service, in any language, reads the rows that list it and no variable the table does not list for it — beyond the standard OTEL_* variables an OpenTelemetry SDK reads on its own, and the options variable of the allocator it links (jemalloc's _RJEM_MALLOC_CONF, which it reads before any of its code runs), which the table neither promises nor refuses. `services` names the services that read each. `readBy` says what reads it: `service`, the service's own code — which lint:service-environment scans in both directions, over each service's crate and every workspace crate it links: a read not listed for that service fails it, and so does a row nothing in it reads; `opentelemetry`, the OpenTelemetry SDK. `providedBy` says what sets each where the launcher runs the service: `launcher` (lint:service-environment checks the service's line of the launcher's boot golden passes it), `image` (the image or its supervisor sets it; checked there too), or `operator` (nothing sets it; an operator may). A service's conformance suite sets only the rows that list it, and exercises each by name; one gateway case also sets a variable a runtime would read for itself (TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS), to show that it changes nothing.

variables.name: JWT_SECRET
variables.effect: The gateway's signing key ring: comma-separated keys of at least 32 characters, whitespace around each ignored. Agent and media tokens are signed with the first key, and a token signed with any key is accepted. Unset, or with a key shorter than 32 characters, the gateway refuses to start.

variables.name: SEMIONT_OIDC_CLIENT_ID
variables.effect: The client id of the service's own account at the issuer: the gateway exchanges its token for the one it reaches the Archivist with, the dispatcher and the Archivist for the agent token each reaches the bus with. Unset, the service refuses to start.

variables.name: SEMIONT_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.effect: That account's secret. Unset, the service refuses to start, and its output never carries the value.

variables.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
variables.effect: The OTLP/HTTP collector spans and metrics are exported to. Unset, with OTEL_CONSOLE_EXPORTER not `true`, nothing is exported.

variables.name: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
variables.effect: The `service.name` exported spans and metrics carry; `semiont-gateway`, `semiont-dispatcher` or `semiont-archivist` when unset.

variables.name: OTEL_SDK_DISABLED
variables.effect: `true` exports nothing, whatever else is set.

variables.name: OTEL_CONSOLE_EXPORTER
variables.effect: `true`, with no OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, writes spans and metrics to the service's output instead of exporting them.

variables.name: OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER
variables.effect: `console` writes metrics to the service's output, while spans still go to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT.

variables.name: OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL
variables.effect: Milliseconds between metric exports; 30000 when unset or not a positive integer.

variables.name: OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY
variables.effect: Milliseconds a finished span waits to be exported in a batch; 5000 when unset.

variables.name: SEMIONT_BUS_LOG
variables.effect: Any non-empty value writes one `[bus <op>] <channel> …` line to the service's output for each frame it sends, accepts, receives or delivers, and each content read.

variables.name: SUPERVISE_EVENTS
variables.effect: The supervisor's events log, one `starting <SUPERVISE_NAME>` line per life of the process. With SUPERVISE_NAME, the service reports `semiont.process.restarts` from it: its lives, less one. Without either, the metric does not exist.

variables.name: SUPERVISE_NAME
variables.effect: The name the supervisor records each life under, in SUPERVISE_EVENTS.
